evidence: The authoritative workbook's Quality Checks!A2:D2 and Internal Quality Checks!A2:D2 require a person's product request rather than a specification/checklist/build recipe; the frozen quality-checks.md:9-10 asks for a cold read and identifies numbered acceptance lists, shall/must tables, feature matrices and build recipes as defects. The frozen task/instruction.md:1 begins 'I'd like a small playground for trying out browser ideas' and immediately explains the workspace and shared-library need. Line 3 states the user's concrete frustration ('The annoying part is losing something that was working') and explains preserving the actual working preview and newer saved work. Lines 5, 7 and 9 remain short prose paragraphs connecting the notes, everyday draft/save use, accessibility and delivery location. There is no acceptance checklist, feature matrix, framework mandate, endpoint list or ordered build procedure in this main brief. The more detailed product rules are coherently placed in the six referenced notes; technical launch facts are in environment/instructions/integration.md, consistent with the frozen template's separate integration note. Task policy.md:5 explicitly leaves layout, control labels, indentation, API routes and request fields open. Adversarial thought experiment: a polished static editor/preview mock could coexist with this natural brief, but its broken behavior cannot establish or defeat this prose-only check; this row does not claim the app or gates work. A conforming alternative with a different frontend/editor library and API layout remains compatible with the request (integration.md:3,5 and policy.md:5), so naturalness is not obtained by prescribing one build.
